analysis: The PR is documentation-only in docs/reference/desktop-control.md. Two changes: the 'Last updated' date moves from 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-26 (line 3), and the GET /control/v1/network row (line 70) now says the public /v1/stats response is 'relayed unchanged including any per-chip by_chip rows and by_chip_window'. No code, auth, crypto, token-handling or transport behavior changes. The documented controls are unchanged: bearer-token auth on every route, Origin and non-loopback rejection, no credential in the renderer, and account-bearer scoping to specific endpoints. The network route is public aggregate data from the coordinator, so relaying per-chip aggregates does not touch A-001, A-008, A-015 or A-016. It also does not weaken TB-002, TB-003 or TB-011 in the supplied context. T-041 was supplied but is not implicated, since this PR does not touch the prefix cache. One open question for integration: 'relayed unchanged' implies the desktop backend does no sanitization of the /v1/stats payload. Whether the Swift code in DesktopBackend.resource bounds the size of the relayed body, or whether the by_chip data could expose per-provider identifiers, could not be checked because that source is not in this batch. Neither is evidenced by the doc. The per-chip aggregate fields are described as public network statistics, so I identified no regression.
